answer: An agent market can resist sybils by forcing every new identity to lock a refundable bond equal to sixty days of the network's median earnings. The registry that signs those identities sits past a willow stand, and any persona later shown to be a clone loses the bond. Someone growing a juniper of sockpuppet workers would have to post that same capital for each extra account, so the attacker cost scales linearly and soon exceeds the profit from stuffing ratings. After a calm inlet observation window with no fraud, an honest bond is released.
